POST /v1/tickets.description: Two steps: the device first creates a conversation of kind `ticket` (POST /v1/conversations) with keys for the requester and the people who may handle it, then calls this with that conversation's id. The ticket's text lives in the sealed conversation. The server picks a handler, starts the TAT clock and notifies them.

request.category: string. Category name for the recipient
request.to_type: string. desk (default) | department | unit | branch | sector
request.to_ref: uuid. The unit when to_type is not desk

response.id: uuid. Same as the ticket's conversation id
response.step: integer. 0 Raised, 1 Assigned, 2 In progress, 3 Resolved, 4 Closed
response.hold: boolean. true while the TAT clock is paused on hold
response.handler: uuid. The person working on it
response.to_type: string. desk | department | unit | branch | sector
response.to_ref: uuid. The unit it was sent to
response.due_at: timestamp. When it is due, counting working hours
response.participant: boolean. In lists: whether I am in the ticket's conversation and can read its sealed thread

errors.400: Unknown priority or recipient, the category does not exist for that recipient, or the conversation was not created first

POST /v1/tickets/{id}/act.description: One endpoint for every step. `do` chooses: assign (set handler/assignees), step (move to Raised, Assigned, In progress, Resolved or Closed), hold, resume, escalate (move to another unit, with a reason) and priority. A person cannot work on a ticket they raised, but may close it. Closing a High priority ticket needs approval (flow f5): resolve it first.
POST /v1/tickets/{id}/act.access: a role with the matching Tickets right (Assign & hand over, Solve, Close, ...)

request.do: string, required. assign | step | hold | resume | escalate | priority
request.to_type: string. escalate: department | unit | branch | sector
request.person: uuid. escalate: who takes it there
request.why: string. escalate: reason, up to 300 characters
request.category: string. escalate: the category at the new place

response.id: uuid. Same as the ticket's conversation id
response.step: integer. 0 Raised, 1 Assigned, 2 In progress, 3 Resolved, 4 Closed
response.hold: boolean. true while the TAT clock is paused on hold
response.handler: uuid. The person working on it
response.to_type: string. desk | department | unit | branch | sector
response.to_ref: uuid. The unit it was sent to
response.due_at: timestamp. When it is due, counting working hours
response.participant: boolean. In lists: whether I am in the ticket's conversation and can read its sealed thread

errors.400: Unknown action, nobody chosen, the person is not in the ticket's conversation, or it is not in the state that action needs
errors.403: own_ticket: you raised it so someone else must work on it
errors.409: already_escalated; needs_approval: closing a High priority ticket needs approval

GET /v1/tickets/settings.description: Working hours, when the clock pauses, when to warn and who to escalate to.

response.timezone: string. IANA zone, Africa/Nairobi by default
response.nearPct: integer. Warn at this percent of the TAT, 10 to 99
response.escalate: string. Who overdue tickets escalate to

PUT /v1/tickets/settings.access: a role with Tickets: Manage TAT settings

request.timezone: string. IANA zone, Africa/Nairobi by default
request.nearPct: integer. Warn at this percent of the TAT, 10 to 99
request.escalate: string. Who overdue tickets escalate to

errors.400: Warning point outside 10 to 99, working hours not like 08:00 to 17:00, or an unknown time zone
